knowledge_cards.claim: Stable perceptual note centre should be estimated separately from attacks, releases, glides and vibrato.
When detuning is severe, nearest-semitone assignment can be ambiguous; sequential musical context can improve target-note inference within the studied vocal task.
A note-level offset can preserve within-note expressive contour better than independent frame quantization; this remains an engineering candidate for rock vocals.
Note-boundary confidence is a safety gate because downstream pitch targets depend on segmentation.
Pitch accuracy, expression preservation and timbral/formant naturalness are separate evaluation axes.
Pitch-shift artifact behavior depends on shift magnitude and algorithm; restoration is a separate processing candidate.
Metric definitions and optimization directions must be audited before numerical results enter project rules.
Vocal correction and priority must be gated by section role and artistic intent.

rule_candidates.when: vocal note centre is suspected inaccurate
rule_candidates.change: estimate stationary/perceptually salient centre separately from transition frames
rule_candidates.test: compare with whole-note mean and manual centre
rule_candidates.cancel: segmentation or stationary-region confidence is low

rule_candidates.change: compare nearest-note, context-informed and guide/score targets when available
rule_candidates.cancel: targets disagree or harmony is atypical

rule_candidates.when: a target note has been accepted
rule_candidates.change: apply the smallest note-level offset while preserving residual within-note contour
stop automatic correction and require manual review

rule_candidates.when: a material pitch shift is required
rule_candidates.change: test formant/timbre restoration as a separate stage
rule_candidates.test: separate F0/voicing metrics and loudness-matched blind timbre A/B
rule_candidates.cancel: timbre or intelligibility worsens despite better F0

rule_candidates.change: hold timing constant and test timing edits separately
gate correction and priority by lead/support/ad-lib role
